note: The Ottoman Empire expanded by absorbing the other Anatolian Turkish beyliks (principalities) — either through conquest or dynastic marriage. Osman I established the beylik in northwestern Anatolia (c. 1300); his successors methodically absorbed neighboring beyliks: Karesi (1345), Germiyan (1390), Hamid (1381), Saruhan (1410). Timur's invasion (1402) temporarily restored some beyliks as Ottoman vassals fled, but Mehmed I reconquered them after the Ottoman civil war (1402–1413). By 1450, the Ottoman state controlled virtually all of Anatolia, with only Karaman holding out until 1468.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Ottoman absorption of the Anatolian beyliks consolidates a unified Turkish state in Anatolia for the first time; the beylik system provided the Ottoman Empire with a diverse pool of administrators, military commanders, and cultural traditions that enriched Ottoman governance; Timur's temporary beylik restoration (1402) delays but cannot reverse the Ottoman consolidation
